explanation:

q: Who called Article 32 of Indian Constitution as "the fundamental of the Fundamental Rights" and "the heart and soul of the Constitution"?
explanation: Dr B.R. Ambedkar called Article 32 the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution in the Constituent Assembly. Moved to the Article 32 row.

notes.text: - **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar**: Art. 32 is "**the very soul of the Constitution and the very heart of it**" – the Article without which the Constitution would be a **nullity** (not Freedom of Speech, Equality, Religion or Property).

exam: APPSC Asst. Director in AP Economic & Statistics 2017
q: The Jurisdiction of a High Court under article 226 cannot be invoked if?
options: The petition raises questions of facts
If the issue is not related to fundamental rights
If there is an alternate and equally efficacious remedy
All the given options are correct
key_text: If there is an alternate and equally efficacious remedy
explanation: A High Court ordinarily declines Art. 226 where an alternative and equally efficacious remedy exists (T.R. Verma). 'All' cannot be right: Art. 226 also covers 'any other purpose', so a non-FR issue is no bar (printed key: all).

notes.text: - **Art. 226 is ordinarily refused** where an **alternative and equally efficacious remedy** exists (rule of prudence; T.R. Verma 1957) or where **disputed questions of fact** need trial; it is **not** barred merely because no FR is involved ("any other purpose").

exam: APPSC Assistant Social, B.C. & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains
q: Any violation of the right of casting a vote permits the aggrieved person the right to approach the High Court under following article of the Constitution
explanation: The right to vote is a constitutional/statutory right, not an FR, so it is enforced in the High Court under Art. 226 (FRs and 'any other purpose'); Art. 32 is only for FRs.

notes.text: - A right that is **not an FR** – e.g. the **right to vote** – is enforced in the **High Court under Art. 226**, not Art. 32.

exam: APPSC Common GS for ADTP, ADILIS, IFS, ATT 2012
q: What Articles of Indian Constitution give powers to a citizen to move the Supreme Court or High Court whenever there is an infringement of Fundamental Right?
explanation: Arts. 32 (Supreme Court) and 226 (High Courts) let a person seek enforcement of FRs.

notes.text: - Citizens move the **Supreme Court (Art. 32)** or the **High Court (Art. 226)** for infringement of FRs – **Arts. 32 and 226** (not 33/227, 34/228). **Only the SC and HCs** issue writs – not "all courts", Parliament or the President.

q: Who is the guardian of the Fundamental Rights of the citizens of India?
explanation: The Judiciary is the guardian of Fundamental Rights (Arts. 32, 226); not the Executive, President or Parliament.

notes.text: - **Guardian / protector of Fundamental Rights = the Judiciary** (Supreme Court as "protector and guarantor") – **not the President**, Parliament, Executive, Cabinet or parties. The **Supreme Court** is also the **custodian / guardian of the Constitution**.

q: The authority to issue writs for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights rests with
explanation: Writs for FRs are issued by the Supreme Court (Art. 32) and the High Courts (Art. 226); of the options only the Supreme Court fits; not all courts, Parliament or the President.

notes.text: - Citizens move the **Supreme Court (Art. 32)** or the **High Court (Art. 226)** for infringement of FRs – **Arts. 32 and 226** (not 33/227, 34/228). **Only the SC and HCs** issue writs – not "all courts", Parliament or the President.

q: Which of the following Articles enables High Courts to issue writs?
explanation: Article 226 enables High Courts to issue writs.

notes.text: - **Article 226** empowers the **High Courts** to issue writs (not 213, 225, 227, 228, 249, 262).

q: The High Courts are empowered for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights under
explanation: Article 226 empowers High Courts to enforce FRs.

notes.text: - **Article 226** empowers the **High Courts** to issue writs (not 213, 225, 227, 228, 249, 262).

q: Regarding the Habeas Corpus, choose the wrong statement out of the given below?
options: Habeas corpus safeguards the Liberty not only of the citizens but also all the persons living within the territory
A writ of Habeas corpus is not to be entertained when a person is committed to Judicial custody or public custody by the competent court
A Petition of Habeas Corpus lies against the executive authority and not available against the private persons
The Habeas Corpus petition cannot be dismissed on the ground of imperfect pleadings
key_text: A Petition of Habeas Corpus lies against the executive authority and not available against the private persons
explanation: Habeas corpus lies against private persons too, so statement 3 is wrong. It protects all persons, is not entertained against lawful judicial custody, and is not dismissed for imperfect pleadings.

notes.text: - **Wrong statement** (asked twice): "Habeas corpus lies against the executive only, not against private persons".
- The **only writ that lies against private persons** as well as the State; safeguards the liberty of **all persons** in the territory, citizens or not.
